title: Hackers attack Ukrainian and Russian emergency apps

paragraphs: Both Ukraine and Russia recently reported that their official emergency alert apps were hit by major cyberattacks, which triggered mass panic through fake notifications.

In Kyiv, citizens received terrifying false warnings about nuclear radiation, chemical threats, and active street fighting, and they were told to stay inside. Ukrainian officials quickly blamed Russian hackers and reassured the public that the actual air defense systems were never compromised. Just hours later, Russia’s Ministry of Emergency Situations reported a similar cyberattack on its own app, which sent out fake alerts with Ukrainian phrasing and offensive language. These attacks target popular mobile apps that millions rely on daily as a backup to air raid sirens.

Experts point out that both countries have advanced hacking teams, and digital sabotage is a key weapon for wearing down morale, creating chaos, and making ordinary people doubt official safety warnings on both sides of the war.

paragraphs: Both Ukraine and Russia say hackers attacked their official emergency apps with fake safety warnings.

People in Ukraine got scary messages on their phones about radiation, chemical danger, and street fights. Officials told everyone it was a fake message from Russian hackers and said their air defense was completely safe. A few hours later, Russia said its own emergency app was also hacked, and people got messages in Ukrainian.

Millions of people use these mobile apps every day to stay safe from real attacks. Experts say these digital attacks are meant to scare people, create confusion, and make people lose trust in official warning systems on both sides of the war.

paragraphs: Hackers attack emergency phone apps in Ukraine and Russia. People get scary fake messages on their phones about a nuclear attack, bad air, and street fights.
Officials in Kyiv tell people not to worry. They say that the messages are fake. A short time later, people in Russia also get strange fake messages.

Millions of people use these apps every day to stay safe. Experts say that hackers do this to scare people, make life hard, and stop people from trusting official safety news. It is a new way for both sides to fight online.
